version.changelog:
shift-handoff-voice 0.1.1

- Initial release of the shift handoff voice skill.
- Converts a written shift handoff checklist into 8–20 labeled voice clips, one per cue.
- Handles outgoing, incoming, and unfinished work priorities.
- Supports both catalog and cloned staff voices, ensuring secure consent and billing checks.
- Executes all operations through the bundled MCP client and strictly follows provided checklists without inventing extra content.
- Provides detailed instructions for authorization, billing, delivery, error recovery, and safe automatic updates.

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised voice-generation workflow, but it also requests broad Beatra account authority, stores a persistent token, sends installation registration data, and silently self-updates installed package files.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local files only for user-authorized uploads and stores Beatra state under ~/.beatra, but it also records host/platform metadata and sends package version, platform, and a stable installation reference to Beatra on first use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill includes default-enabled silent automatic updates that check remote discovery and replace package-owned installed files without separate per-update confirmation, even though it documents checksum, path, rollback, and disable controls.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions mostly require user-visible planning and approval before paid clone or speech calls, but the bundled client exposes a raw MCP call interface without enforcing a skill-specific allowlist, relying on instructions and the remote service to keep use in scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a shared full-scope Device Token in ~/.beatra/credentials.json with POSIX permission checks and a documented 15-day idle lifetime, but that credential covers more Beatra capabilities than this single voice workflow needs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Voice synthesis, voice selection, optional voice cloning, uploads, task polling, and billing checks are coherent with creating shift handoff audio clips, but the authorization scope in scripts/authorize.py also includes unrelated image, video, music, broad artifact, task cancellation, and wallet spending capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable connecting a Beatra account to this agent, storing a shared Beatra device token on disk, allowing Beatra installation registration telemetry, and accepting default silent package updates. Consider disabling automatic updates with the documented command and revoking the device in the Beatra Console when done.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The concern is supported in part: the manifest discloses Beatra MCP authentication and credential_file, but the artifact does not present a narrow permission model for shell execution, network calls, file writes, credential storage, and local upload behavior.
[TP4] unexpected: Partly supported: remote Beatra auth, uploads, tasks, and billing are coherent with the workflow, but the raw MCP client, broad account scopes, telemetry, uninstall handling, and self-update behavior exceed the narrow voice-clip description.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported for automatic updates and broad credential scope: the artifact explicitly enables silent self-updates by default and requests scopes beyond speech, voice, upload, and task recovery needs.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported for self-update and overbroad package-management behavior; downgraded from malicious because the update path is disclosed and contains source, checksum, path, rollback, and package-owned-file constraints.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported: default-enabled silent updates and installation registration are documented, but they are not part of the core voice task and occur without a per-run approval prompt.
[PE3] expected: Persistent credential storage is expected for a remote paid media service and is documented with file-permission guidance, but it remains concerning because the token is shared and broad-scoped.
[RA1] unexpected: Supported as a Review concern, not malicious: scripts/mcp_client.py includes update commands and default automatic self-replacement of package files, with safety checks but without per-update user approval.
